qt: to the Commission Ton Diepeveen (PfE) Subject:

The Commission’s proposal for the EU Inc. appears to take insufficient account of the position of pledgees and mortgagees in the event of insolvency. Under the proposal, they would be unable to lodge a separate claim against the insolvent EU Inc., and their rights as preferential creditors would not be safeguarded, or would be inadequately safeguarded. This could undermine legal certainty for lenders and make it more difficult for EU Inc. companies to access finance. 1.
Can the Commission confirm exactly what rights pledgees and mortgagees have under the proposed insolvency proceedings, and how their existing security rights would be protected?

How does the Commission ensure that the proposed regime does not lead to a situation in which banks and other lenders regard EU Inc. companies as posing a greater risk than companies incorporated as national legal forms, particularly in Member States where pledgees and mortgagees enjoy specific preferential rights?

Is the Commission prepared to amend the proposed insolvency rules to ensure that pledgees and mortgagees can fully exercise their security rights and that EU Inc. companies do not suffer a competitive disadvantage vis-à-vis national company forms?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (16.11.2026) Chapter X of the Commission’s EU Inc. proposal1 contains procedural rules, which are aimed to ensure an expedited liquidation of those EU Inc. companies that qualify as ‘innovative startups’. For EU Inc.s that are concerned by this Chapter, national insolvency proceedings shall be conducted in compliance with the unified provisions in this Chapter. These rules ensure an easily ascertainable opening condition, the use of digital communication, the involvement of an insolvency practitioner, procedural simplification of lodging and admitting claims, a brief overall duration for the procedure (six months, as a rule), and new tools for asset realisation (e-auction platforms). Apart from these questions, all other aspects of insolvency proceedings, including the substantive issue of the ranking of claims (e.g. the rights and privileges of secured creditors in the context of insolvency proceedings) are left to the applicable national insolvency law and are not touched by the proposed provisions. Similarly, the proposed Chapter X is without prejudice to Regulation (EU) 2015/848 on insolvency proceedings, which applies to determine international jurisdiction and applicable law in insolvency proceedings. This means that the rules on applicable law of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 on insolvency proceedings will remain relevant, including the provision that protects third parties’ property rights (Article 8). Consequently, the rights of mortgagees and pledgees are not affected by the proposed Chapter X of the EU Inc. Regulation.
1 Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on the 28th regime corporate legal
